subject.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall

question: Should OpenClaw accept SourceActor/sourceActor as the public plugin, message, and memory attribution contract for this stack once the queued propagation bug and merge conflicts are fixed?
rationale: The PR creates plugin-facing API and prompt/memory semantics that external plugins may rely on after release, so maintainers must choose the long-term naming, scalar mirrors, and privacy boundary.

options.title: Approve After Propagation Fix
options.body: Keep the SourceActor direction, require the queued follow-up fix and rebase, then review the memory PR after the prerequisite stack lands.

options.title: Rename Or Narrow Contract
options.body: Ask for a revised public API before release if maintainers want fewer scalar mirrors, different naming, or stricter privacy boundaries.

options.title: Pause The Stack
options.body: Leave the PR draft or close later if participant attribution should be structurally stored before being exposed as best-effort context.

recommendation.title: Approve After Propagation Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the SourceActor direction, require the queued follow-up fix and rebase, then review the memory PR after the prerequisite stack lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing evidence is recent ownership of the follow-up runner, inbound context, and plugin descriptor context surfaces involved in the public contract decision.
